subject: Regional inference competitive briefing & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Harris <david.harris@globex.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12 09:12 -0700
Subject: Regional inference competitive briefing & next steps

Thanks again for carving out time this morning — appreciate the honest convo. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on a compact test plan.

Call highlights (short):
- Your goals: consistent sub-200ms p95 for EU/US traffic for short prompts (~50 tokens) and predictable throughput for bursts (200 rps).
- Competitive space: you mentioned tests vs Bedrock endpoints and a managed Vertex-like setup (GCP).
- Constraints: strict EU data residency for GDPR-regulated datasets, and procurement prefers vendors that support VPC/private endpoints and SOC2 evidence.

Where Redwood helps (summary):
- Multi-mode deployment: hosted API for quick evaluation, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, and Private/VPC for EU residency and audit controls.
- Performance controls: workload-aware batching + KV prefix caching to reduce tail latency on conversational patterns.
- Cost/levers: quantization profiles + autoscaling policies to trade latency vs cost during bursts.
- Reliability: smart routing with region-aware fallbacks so you don’t hit cold-capacity failures during peak.

Proposed next steps (we recommend running a 48-hour regional comparison):
1) We run simultaneous synthetic tests from your EU and US egress points (we can use the IPs you provide) to measure p50/p95/p99 for 50/256 token requests.
2) We compare against Bedrock/Vertex results you already have (if you share the test config) and provide a per-region cost estimate and unit economics.
3) For EU residency validation, we’ll stand up a Private demo in your EU VPC or a Hosted EU endpoint with data-at-rest controls and provide SOC2 artifacts.

Can you confirm: 1) which regions you want prioritized (EU/US/APAC), 2) whether you can share the Bedrock/Vertex test scripts or the exact payloads, and 3) a preferred 48-hour window for tests?

I’ve attached a short test-plan draft and a sample latency-capture CSV we’ll use for the baseline. Rishi and Sergio will own the test execution; I’ll coordinate logistics and procurement asks.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: David Harris <david.harris@globex.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Cole <emma.cole@globex.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional inference competitive briefing & next steps

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. Couple quick clarifications before we lock windows:

- Prioritization: EU first (Ireland), then US-East. APAC is lower priority but we'd like a separate follow-up if results look promising.
- Bedrock/Vertex test artifacts: we can share our JMeter scripts and the request payloads — I'll drop them in the shared drive link if you confirm receipt.
- Residency: procurement will need confirmation that (a) data stays in-region for inference, and (b) we can route logs to our EU logging account. Is that supported in the Hosted EU endpoint or do we need Private?

Also, what’s your expected p99 behavior under a burst scenario? We saw spikes with Bedrock during warm-up periods and want to avoid that for customer-facing flows.

Can you also confirm whether you can provide temporary test API keys scoped to an IP allowlist and limited qps? That will make it easier for our infra team to kick off tests.

-David
David Harris
Director, Platform Engineering | Globex AI
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: David Harris <david.harris@globex.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13 08:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional inference competitive briefing & next steps

Hi David — quick technical note and proposed test matrix.

Short answers to your questions:
- EU residency: Hosted EU endpoints keep inference data in-region for request handling and do not persist payloads beyond retention windows; for full control we recommend Private (VPC) which guarantees tenancy and log routing. We will provide SOC2 artifacts and an audit checklist.
- Burst p99: Our continuous-batching + prefix cache typically keeps p99 within ~1.2–2x of p95 for short prompts once warm; cold-start p99s are higher but we mitigate with pre-warming and smart routing. We’ll include warm-up runs in the plan.

Proposed 48-hour test matrix (attached as PDF):
- Regions: EU (eu-west-1) and US (us-east-1)
- Payload shapes: short prompt (50 tokens) and longer prompt (256 tokens)
- Concurrency profile: steady 50 rps, burst windows to 250 rps for 2 minutes every 15 minutes
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, token cost, GPU utilization (for Dedicated runs)
- Comparison targets: Bedrock (config you provide) and GCP Vertex (if you have it)

Files attached: redwood-regional-test-plan-20260913.pdf, sample-latency-traces-20260912.csv. I also attached a small script to collect client-side timestamps so we can align traces.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Globex provides the Bedrock/Vertex scripts and an allowlist IP for test keys.
2) We create short-lived scoped API keys (IP-limited) for both Hosted EU and Hosted US endpoints; if you want Private we can scope the work and timeline separately.
3) Schedule an ops handoff call — I propose Monday 09/14 10:00 PT for runbook walk-through.

If that works, we’ll provision keys and finalize the timelines.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Harris <david.harris@globex.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13 11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional inference competitive briefing & next steps

All — thanks Rishi. David — we can absolutely provide IP-scoped, time-limited API keys for the Hosted EU and US endpoints. I’ll initiate the HubSpot deal stage update and attach the test plan to the record.

I scheduled the ops handoff for Mon 2026-09-14 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Agenda: test runbook, key distribution, and guardrails for warm-up and failure modes. Please let me know if you need a different time.

For procurement: Sergio, can you prepare the SOC2 artifact bundle and a short note on data-retention defaults for Hosted EU? Lauren, can you draft a short procurement checklist that calls out Private/VPC option timelines and one-time setup costs? I’ll attach both to the HubSpot record.

David — we’ll also run a preliminary 2-hour warm-up window in your chosen EU location the day before the 48-hour run to capture cold->warm behavior.

—
Marissa
From: David Harris <david.harris@globex.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Cole <emma.cole@globex.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-16 15:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional inference competitive briefing & next steps

Thanks — that timeline looks good. We confirmed EU (Ireland) IPs and will upload the Bedrock/Vertex jmeter scripts to the shared Drive folder tonight.

Preferred testing windows:
- Warm-up: 2026-09-17 08:00–10:00 UTC (EU warm-up)
- 48-hour run: 2026-09-18 00:00 UTC to 2026-09-20 00:00 UTC

Please generate the two time-limited keys and share them with our infra alias ops@globex.ai on the allowlisted IPs. Also — if you can, include a small sample trace capture (client timestamps + server-side IDs) so we can correlate traces with our internal dashboards.

Appreciate the SOC2/retention note and the procurement checklist — that will speed review. Looking forward to seeing the comparative numbers (esp p99 under bursts).

-David
